content:
maria: noticed a wave of OOMs in prod-serving starting around the 20% canary rollout
james: same. Staging saw a tiny bump yesterday but we ignored it. Prod is hitting longctx jobs (seqlen 4096) and OOMs spike.
kai: I ran a quick bisect on the canary diff. Two suspicious merges: a) kernel-routing heuristics (9f3a2b6) b) batching-router shuffle (4ae5bd1). Both landed in the same release.
maria: logs show repeated failures in kv_cache allocation:
```
ERROR runtime::kv_cache: allocation failed: requested 6.5GiB remaining 2.1GiB
stacktrace: runtime::kv::Heaplet::alloc -> runtime::kv::evict -> runtime::cache::insert
```
ananya: perf profile from a repro run (staging, seqlen 4096):
```
kv_cache::evict 45.3%
alloc::Heaplet::alloc 22.1%
kernel_select::choose 12.4%
batching::router::dispatch 8.7%
```
chris: interesting that kernel_select shows up. The routing change started preferring larger-kernel backends for throughput; might be causing larger per-request kvcache footprints.
james: can reproduce locally with a mixed seqlen workload. When kernel routing picks 'big-kernel' we see slab fragmentation: many small allocations across different heaplets instead of coalesced pages.
kai: hypothesis: batching-router change moved some requests to a different worker pool which uses a different heaplet stride. When combined with the kernel selection change, allocations land on different arenas -> fragmentation -> OOM.
maria: @deploy-bot did the canary rollback already? can't see traffic shift in the dashboard.
deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated at 1949502500, rolling to previous config. :information_source:
ci-bot: perf test seqlen=2048 shows +18% p99 and +12% mem for the new routing combo. Link: https://ci.internal/perf/19495
ananya: attached a small reproducer script (ran in staging):
```
# run longctx workload
for i in {1..30}; do ./client --model oak-16k --seq 4096 --batch 2; sleep 1; done
```
james: quick mitigation: limit batching router max_batch_tokens to 4096 and force kernel-selection to prefer 'small-kernel' for sequences >= 2048. That reduces fragmentation in my tests.
chris: we should do a rollback on the kernel-routing heuristic first. It seems higher risk. If deploy-bot already rolled back, monitor.
maria: filing a rollback + hotfix plan. I'll open the PR to revert 9f3a2b6 and a followup to add seqlen-aware allocator coalescing.
kai: also adding a CI job that runs heavy longctx mem tests in parallel (flaky now) and a fuzz eviction test to catch fragmentation.
ananya: note: the eviction metric shows repeated tiny evicts that don't free contiguous pages, causing slow memory growth. A targeted compaction after aggressive evict might help but it's risky.
james: patch ready to pin kernel-selection for canary to old behavior. Will push PR and request review: PR: https://git.internal/r/PR-8213
maria: good. Also add a dashboard delta: kv_slab_frag_percent and slab_free_runs so SRE can alert earlier.
chris: SRE alert rule created: kv_slab_frag_percent > 30% for 5m -> paging the eng-runtime on-call.
ci-bot: perf test results updated: after pinning kernel-selection locally, p99 back to baseline, mem down ~7%.
deploy-bot: revert PR merged at 1949502705 and rollout set to 0% canary, rolling new stable. :white_check_mark:
maria: monitor for 30m then re-open canary slowly. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
james: followup: will add allocator coalescing telemetry and a small unit test for different heaplet strides.
ananya: I'll add the reproducer to the perf-suite so we don't regress silently.
chris: closing loop: if we still see OOMs after rollback, we'll revert batching-router too. For now, ops keep an eye on memory graphs and evict logs.
deploy-bot: final status: rollback complete, canary 0% -> stable restored at 1949502799
